# The work between `0.1.0-2.x` and the next rung

**Generated by `tools/gen_version_ladder.qu`. Do not edit.**
Regenerating is how you find out whether this is still true; it
is derived from the same scrape as the rung table, so it cannot
disagree with it.

The project version is the lowest rung any function occupies.
**163 functions sit on `0.1.0-2.x` (Next).**
When the last reaches `0.1.0-3.a` (Alpha), the project advances to it. That is
checkable by re-running this tool rather than by anyone's
judgement, which is the point.

## Three jobs, cheapest first

**29 are ALREADY TESTED in Qu** and only invisible
to the counter, which refuses to count a dotted call in a `.rs`
file because `v.push(` is Rust's own method and `x.mean(` inside
an embedded Qu program is not, and the preceding character
cannot separate them. **The coverage exists.** Each needs only a
small `.qu` test to make it countable. Marked **[countable]**.

**7 are genuinely untested** -- every dotted hit
is a Rust host method. Marked **[rust-only]**.

**The remaining 127 have no evidence of any
kind** and need tests written.

The split above is HAND-CONFIRMED and stored in
`versions/triage.tsv`. Do not re-derive it with a script. Two
attempts were made: one cleared 35 of 36 uniformly, which is how
it was caught, since nothing legitimately does that; the next
scored 12 out of 12 against hand-read names and still got
`viterbi` and `diff` wrong, because it stopped searching after
25 lines and none of the twelve sat further away than that.

No function below appears in `versions/garbage.tsv`, so none
of this is work that should not happen.
